paragraphs: Northland and Southmark will meet next week in the neutral city of Arlen to discuss turning the 30-day Vell Valley ceasefire into a longer agreement, according to statements from both foreign ministries.

The truce began on September 20 and has largely held, though monitors reported sporadic small-arms fire near the river crossings. Northland's foreign ministry said the talks would cover a withdrawal line for heavy weapons and the reopening of two road crossings closed since the spring.

Southmark's deputy foreign minister, Ilse Varga, said her government wants international observers to stay in the valley, a demand Northland has resisted. Northland officials said they would bring proposals on prisoner exchanges and on the return of about 12,000 displaced residents, without saying whether they would accept observers.

Shipping firms that use the Vell estuary are watching closely. Traffic there fell by roughly a third during the summer fighting, according to the regional port authority, and insurers raised premiums for ships calling at nearby ports.
The ceasefire expires on October 20. Diplomats said a short extension could be agreed at the start of the three-day meeting to give negotiators more time, but neither side has committed to one.
Federal Reserve Governor Ana Hale said cooling inflation leaves room for one more quarter-point rate cut before the end of the year, speaking to a business group in Cleveland on Thursday.

Hale pointed to three straight months of slower price growth for services and described the labor market as cooling but not cracking, with no sign of a sharp rise in layoffs. Analysts quoted by Fixture Markets called her remarks the clearest signal yet from a board member that a December cut is likely. Hale joined the Fed board in 2024 and is seen by investors as a centrist.

Not every official agrees. Two regional bank presidents said last week that they want more months of data before cutting again, and minutes from the September meeting showed several participants worried inflation could stall above the 2 percent target.

Two-year Treasury yields fell about five basis points after the speech and futures markets priced a higher chance of a December cut, while mortgage rates, which track longer-term yields, were little changed on the day. The next policy meeting is October 27 to 28, and Hale did not say whether she would support a move then.
